policy: No asset is bundled unless its redistribution rights are recorded and approved.

sources.title: Islamic AI Challenge — official home
sources.use: Tracks, dates, deliverables, participation rules, and challenge framing.
sources.license_action: Use as competition documentation; do not reproduce site content beyond necessary project references.
sources.notes: Official challenge page states a complete runnable product is required, with operating documents, source/license log, presentation, short video, and permitted public code.

sources.title: Islamic AI Challenge — terms
sources.use: Rights, submission licenses, privacy, human evaluation, and documentation obligations.
sources.license_action: Read and comply; obtain rights for every bundled component.
sources.notes: Do not treat the challenge submission license as a license for third-party data. Keep the project’s own source and component register.

sources.title: Tanzil Quran Text — text license
sources.use: Production Arabic Qur’an text, imported verbatim and indexed separately from normalized search text.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0, with Tanzil-specific requirements
sources.license_action: Include attribution and link to tanzil.net; do not alter verbatim text; preserve the copyright notice.
sources.notes: Use checksums and keep a canonical copy. Search normalization must never overwrite display text.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus — data download
sources.use: Optional morphology and syntax features; not required for the first verification MVP.
sources.license: GNU public license stated by the project; review project terms before redistribution.
sources.license_action: Keep optional until the license and research/non-commercial conditions are reviewed for this use.
sources.notes: Do not make the core product dependent on this annotation during the competition prototype.

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus — FAQ
sources.use: Understand accuracy, citation, and research-use context.
sources.license_action: Read alongside the download and license pages; record any additional conditions.
sources.notes: The FAQ describes ongoing correction and research/non-commercial conditions.

sources.title: Quran.com — terms and conditions
sources.use: Potential external reference link only, subject to permission.
sources.license_action: Do not scrape or bundle Quran.com content under the current plan.
sources.notes: The terms describe service content as personal, non-commercial content and include third-party material.

sources.title: Sunnah.com — about, sources, numbering, and grading
sources.use: Research reference and source-discovery only until explicit redistribution permission is obtained.
sources.license_action: Do not scrape or redistribute Hadith text from the site without written permission or a separate clearly applicable license.
sources.notes: The site explains its source and numbering process and cautions that Hadith resources should not be used as do-it-yourself fiqh.

sources.title: OpenITI Corpus
sources.license_action: Check rights per text and per underlying source before copying or redistributing anything.
sources.notes: The corpus contains texts from multiple sources and notes variation in fidelity, including OCR and manual transcription differences.

sources.title: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
sources.use: Reference for attribution obligations when a future corpus is CC BY 4.0.
sources.license_action: For every CC BY asset, give credit, link the license, and indicate changes.
sources.notes: This is a license reference, not a grant of rights to any particular Islamic content.

sources.title: Sunnah.com official API
sources.use: Runtime retrieval of hadith text, numbering, and grading with attribution.
sources.license_action: Request an API key via the project's GitHub issue tracker and request the offline dump only with a clear, stated use. Comply with their terms.
sources.notes: Wrapping at runtime is different from bundling: do not commit the returned text into the public repo unless permission allows it. Offline access is available on request.

sources.title: Quran Foundation / Quran.com Content API
sources.use: Runtime access to verses, translations, tafsir, audio, and search via app credentials (no user login for Content APIs).
sources.license_action: Register an app, use pre-live then production credentials, and honor the service terms. Do not redistribute content as your own dataset.
sources.notes: Quran.com website terms describe content as personal, non-commercial and restrict copying and derivative works. Registering for the official API is the compliant path; scraping the site is not.

sources.title: fawazahmed0/hadith-api
sources.use: Possible bulk hadith + translation + grading source for indexing.
sources.license_action: Treat the Unlicense as covering the code. Independently verify the licensing and provenance of each bundled translation before redistribution.
sources.notes: The licensing of the underlying texts is openly disputed in the project's own issue tracker. Use with a documented provenance and attribution policy.

sources.title: Saheeh International English translation
sources.use: Candidate English translation — must be license-cleared before use.
sources.license: Copyright, published by Dar Abul Qasim / Abul-Qasim Publishing House; some reprints carry a permissive no-changes notice.
sources.license_action: Confirm permissions in writing with the rights holder for the exact edition before displaying or redistributing it. Popularity is not a license.
sources.notes: A widely circulated reprint (The Qur'an Project / Maktabah edition) states that no rights are reserved provided no changes are made and the publisher is notified — but this must be verified for the specific edition used.

sources.title: Public-domain / permissive Qur'an translation candidates
sources.use: Fallback translations that may have simpler redistribution terms than modern copyrighted ones.
sources.license_action: Verify the copyright status of each translation and of the exact digital edition before bundling.
sources.notes: Older translations (e.g. early 20th-century English works) are often public domain, but digitized editions may still carry publisher rights. Check per edition.

sources.title: Islamic AI Challenge — eligibility and IP notes
sources.use: Reminder of submission requirements and IP handling.
sources.license_action: Keep the component register and rights disclosures current; do not bundle unlicensed content.
sources.notes: The competition requires a rights log and prohibits uploading third-party materials without authorization.
